title: Region choice UX, consent language and customer comms playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This playbook captures the recommended UX choices, sample consent/legal copy, operator checks, telemetry event names, and a staged comms/rollout plan for surfacing region selection (customer-driven region choice) and opt-in residency guarantees in the Redwood Private/Dedicated onboarding flows.

Audience:
- Product/UX: implement UI patterns and copy
- Legal: sign off on consent language and data processing notes
- Solutions/SE: customer-facing comms and onboarding checklist
- Engineering/Infra: feature flags, API contract, telemetry, and rollout automation
- Support/CS: FAQ and escalation playbook

High-level requirements (non-exhaustive):
1) Customers must be able to choose a preferred region (or accept default) during provisioning and from Console settings.
2) Choosing a region triggers binding residency constraints for requests and (where applicable) model artifacts and logs.
3) Consent must be explicit and auditable (timestamped).
4) Operators need clear rollback and exception paths (temporary failover during incidents).
5) Telemetry must show intent, enforcement, and violations for audits.

Product decisions recommended:
- Opt-in vs opt-out: default to region-aware routing (best-effort regional routing) but require explicit opt-in for "registered residency" (contracted, pinned infrastructure) that creates enforceable guarantees — because many customers want strong guarantees and legal commitments.
- Two-mode UI: 
  * Quick mode (default): "Prefer region X" — advisory; lower friction for self-serve.
  * Residency mode (contracted): "Require data residency in X" — requires contractual consent and provisioning of pinned capacity.
- Surface consequences up-front: cost delta, latency tradeoffs, and provisioning lead time.

Suggested Console UI flows and copy snippets (feel free to A/B):
1) Provisioning step (self-serve)
  Title: Choose your data region
  Copy: "Select where request processing and short-term operational data (logs, traces) are stored. Choosing a region helps meet data locality requirements. For enforceable residency guarantees (required for contracts), select 'Registered residency' below."
  Controls: dropdown for region, radio for mode: [Prefer region] / [Registered residency (contract required)]
  Legal checkbox (registered residency): "I understand choosing Registered residency triggers capacity reservation and a binding residency commitment as described in the contract and the data processing addendum."
2) Settings page (change region)
  - Warn about migration windows, potential downtime, and re-provisioning lead time.
  - For customers in Registered residency, require Support approval and create an audit ticket automatically.
3) Minimal Consent Wording (short)
  - "By selecting Registered residency you request that Redwood keep processing for this workload confined to the selected region(s). Some narrow operational activities (e.g., control-plane indexing, billing) may still occur outside the region; see the Data Processing Addendum."
4) Expanded Legal Copy (detailed) — work with Legal before shipping.

API & flags (implementation guidance):
- New account-level property: residency.mode = [advisory|registered] and residency.region = [region-code].
- Admin API endpoints: PATCH /v1/accounts/{id}/residency {mode, region, requested_at, accepted_tos_version}
- Operator flag: enable_force_failover = boolean (used only for emergency cross-region failovers)
- Degraded fallback policy must be explicit: for Registered residency customers, fallback should be last-resort and require an audit entry and customer-notify step (unless emergency=true).

Telemetry and auditability (required events):
- residency.choice.requested (account_id, user_id, mode, region, ui_or_api, timestamp)
- residency.choice.accepted (… , tos_version, contract_id if applicable)
- residency.enforcement.start (resource_id, region, enforced=true/false, timestamp, reason)
- residency.enforcement.violation (resource_id, request_id, actual_region, intended_region, severity, timestamp)
- residency.migration.started / residency.migration.completed (with job id, duration, downtime_estimate)
- residence.fallback.invoked (account_id, operator_id, reason, ticket_id)
Events should be indexed for audit reports and exported to the Compliance S3 bucket. All events must include a human-readable reason and a link to the originating change (console link / ticket / PR).

Operator checklist for onboarding Registered residency (quick start):
- Verify contract and DPA signed => attach contract_id to account record
- Reserve capacity in the target region (dedicated/pinned pool allocation)
- Run preflight: model artifact location, KV cache locality, blobstore residency scan
- Enable enforcement policies in router (route_by_region=true for account)
- Sanity test: synthetic requests from an IP in-region and from an external IP to verify routing and enforcement logs
- Confirm telemetry events recorded (residency.choice.accepted, residency.enforcement.start)

Staged rollout plan (recommended):
Phase 0 — internal beta (2 weeks): feature flags on dev and staging, internal SE teams test with synthetic customers
Phase 1 — limited partner pilot (1 month): 2–3 customers with negotiated contracts; manual operator provisioning and close SRE support
Phase 2 — self-serve registered residency (60–90 days): automation of capacity reservation, contract attachment flows, GA console sections
Phase 3 — enforcement hardening and audit export (ongoing): retention SLA, third-party audit evidence bundle generator

Customer communication templates (email + Console banner):
- Pre-provision notice (email): short note when a customer requests registered residency describing lead time and contact for contracting
- Provision complete (email + Console): "Your account is now configured for Registered residency in <region>. If you have compliance questions, reply to this message or contact your SE."
- Violation notification (automated): clearly show what happened, why, and next steps (ticket link).

Testing matrix (sample cases):
- Happy path: user selects advisory region, traffic routes in-region where possible, no enforcement flags recorded.
- Registered happy path: user selects registered residency, capacity reserved, enforcement true, no violations during 24h soak test.
- Violation simulation: force a router failure to emulate cross-region fallback — ensure residency.enforcement.violation is emitted and ticket created.
- Migration story: change region for advisory account — verify zero-downtime for ephemeral workloads; for registered, verify migration job kicks off and migration.* events recorded.

Rollback and emergency guidance:
- Rolling back a Registered residency change requires: operator approval, explicit ticket that records reason, and recording of residency.choice.* events with previous state.
- Emergency cross-region failover: require operator to set emergency=true and post a standardized incident note; postmortem must include root-cause and whether fallback was invoked.

Open questions / decisions pending (for leadership/legal):
- Which exact set of control-plane activities are permissible outside region for Registered residency? (Legal to finalize)
- Contract templates: add explicit downtime and failover clauses? (Sales/Legal)
- Billing model for Registered residency (one-time reservation fee vs premium monthly) — Product to decide.

Appendix: quick copy variants for A/B tests
A) Short: "Choose a region to process your requests. Registered residency requires a contract and reserved capacity."
B) Focus on compliance: "Keep processing and short-term operational data in the selected territory to meet regulatory obligations."
C) Simpler: "Prefer region: <dropdown>. Want a guaranteed residency? Toggle Registered residency (contact required)."

Next steps (owners):
- UX: prototype console flows and send to Legal for copy review (owner: Priya) — due 2024-11-01
- Legal: produce short and long consent language + DPA clause suggestions (owner: Mark) — due 2024-11-08
- Infra: API contract and telemetry events implemented behind feature flag (owner: Evan) — due 2024-12-01
- Solutions/SE: draft customer comm templates and pilot onboarding checklist (owner: Carlos) — due 2024-11-15

Notes: This document is intentionally UX-first — many existing residency docs focus on routing and enforcement. We need a concise, customer-facing treatment that ties the legal/contracting path to the console experience to avoid surprises during sales/onboarding.

Revision history:
- 2024-10-17: initial draft by Aisha Kapoor
- 2024-10-24: added telemetry schema and sample API contract (Evan)
- 2025-03-12: updated operator checklist and rollout timelines after pilot feedback (Priya, Carlos)
